title: Two neighbors
text: Two power companies share a river, but plan their work without seeing each other. The Savannah River is the border: Georgia Power builds on the Georgia side, Dominion Energy on the South Carolina side.

title: Their plans
text: Dominion plans 54 jobs. Georgia Power plans 60. Nobody lines them up. MrGridy put every one of them on one map, from their public filings.

title: Where they collide
text: Of 2,580 possible pairs, only 50 are within a crew's morning drive, forty kilometers. Two of them touch outright.

title: The best match
text: These two jobs touch. One crew, one yard, one permit instead of two. Dominion's Okatie to McIntosh 115 kilovolt Tie, and Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh expansion. Both are under construction at the same time for about 7 months.

title: What it saves
text: What working together could save: roughly $2.1 million across all 50 matches, somewhere between $1 million and $3.1 million. It is an estimate. Georgia Power does not publish its project costs, so real savings could be higher.

title: When a storm comes
text: About 51 hours before Hurricane Helene arrived, MrGridy predicted where lines would break for both companies, and compared it with what happened. It simulated the storm 10,000 times, with physics.

title: Fix it together
text: Working together, power comes back about 8.1 hours sooner, and 2.6 hours sooner for people who rely on powered medical equipment. Shared staging yards and crews go to the nearest repair zone first, whichever company owns it. Two neighbors, one plan.

title: Corridor fly-through
text: This is the number one match, near Rincon, Georgia. In teal, DESC's Okatie to McIntosh 115 kilovolt Tie. In orange, Georgia Power's Plant McIntosh expansion. Here the two projects touch, so their outages have to be planned together. They could share outage coordination, right-of-way, access roads and permits. One staging yard, right beside both jobs, would serve both crews. And for about 7 months, both crews are due to be here at the same time.

title: Storm crew briefing: Helene
text: Storm crew briefing for Hurricane Helene. On the Georgia side, the heaviest outages are expected in Richmond County, Chatham County and Columbia County, with about 757,000 customers out across Georgia at the peak. On the South Carolina side, watch Charleston County, Aiken County and Greenville County, with about 355,000 customers out statewide. The simulation expects roughly 400 damaged transmission sections on Georgia Power's system and none on DESC's. No single yard reaches both sides quickly for this storm, so each utility stages on its own side and shares updates. Vulnerable areas first. Start near Pierce County, where about 1,700 residents rely on powered medical equipment, then Lowndes County and Jeff Davis County. Working together, power comes back about 8.1 hours sooner. Zone order is live on the MrGridy map. Stay safe.

title: Storm crew briefing: Helene (español)
text: Informes para las cuadrillas sobre la tormenta del huracán Helene. Del lado de Georgia, se esperan los mayores apagones en Richmond County, Chatham County y Columbia County, con unos 757,000 clientes sin servicio en todo Georgia en el punto máximo. Del lado de South Carolina, vigilen Charleston County, Aiken County y Greenville County, con unos 355,000 clientes sin servicio en todo el estado. La simulación espera aproximadamente 400 secciones de transmisión dañadas en el sistema de Georgia Power y ninguna en el de DESC. Ningún campamento llega rápido a ambos lados para esta tormenta, por lo que cada empresa de servicios públicos se instala en su propio lado y comparte actualizaciones. Las áreas vulnerables primero. Comiencen cerca de Pierce County, donde unos 1,700 residentes dependen de equipos médicos eléctricos, luego sigan en Lowndes County y Jeff Davis County. Trabajando juntos, la energía regresa unas 8.1 horas antes. El orden de las zonas está activo en el mapa de MrGridy. Manténganse seguros.

title: Storm crew briefing: Matthew
text: Storm crew briefing for Hurricane Matthew. On the Georgia side, the heaviest outages are expected in Chatham County, Glynn County and Effingham County, with about 228,000 customers out across Georgia at the peak. On the South Carolina side, watch Charleston County, Berkeley County and Horry County, with about 619,000 customers out statewide. The simulation expects roughly 11 damaged transmission sections on Georgia Power's system and 21 on DESC's. Both utilities stage jointly at GA 25 bridge over the Savannah River, which reaches four repair zones within 58 minutes. Vulnerable areas first. Start near Jasper County, where about 3,100 residents rely on powered medical equipment, then Beaufort County and Colleton County. Working together, power comes back about 12 hours sooner. Zone order is live on the MrGridy map. Stay safe.

title: Spark
text: a single subtle electric spark crackle, short and clean, close up, no music

title: Grid hum
text: a soft low electrical substation hum, steady and calm, seamless loop, no music
